requirement: FastAPI get_db dependency generator using try...finally: db.close() to ensure SQLAlchemy sessions are always closed after request execution, including on HTTP exceptions and errors.
skeleton: FastAPI dependency generator get_db() managing SQLAlchemy Session lifecycle.
caption: A FastAPI service instrumented to make the SQLAlchemy session lifecycle observable. The module creates a StaticPool engine over in-memory SQLite, a DeclarativeBase, and an Item table with integer id and non-null name. A SessionMetrics class holds two class-level counters, created and closed, and reset_db drops and recreates the schema while zeroing both. TrackedSession subclasses Session and overrides close to increment the closed counter before delegating to the parent; the sessionmaker is built with class_=TrackedSession. The get_db dependency increments created, opens one session, yields it, and closes it in a finally clause, so teardown runs whether the route returns or raises. The pydantic models are ItemCreate with a name and ItemResponse with id and name from ORM attributes. Routes: GET /session-metrics returns both counters as JSON; POST /items adds, commits, refreshes, and answers 201; GET /items lists every row; GET /error-http raises HTTPException 400 with detail Custom HTTP Error; POST /uncommitted-leak adds an item and then raises HTTPException 400 before any commit, so the pending row is discarded with the session; POST /items-validated raises HTTPException 422 with detail Invalid item name when the name is FAIL_TRIGGER, before adding anything, and otherwise persists and answers 201. Every request gets its own session, and the closed count rises by one after both a successful request and a request that raised.

plan.intent: Guarantee that every request's database session is closed
constraints: One session is opened per request and closed in a finally clause
The closed count rises after a successful request and after one that raised HTTPException 400
A row added before a raised error is never committed
The validated create raises HTTPException 422 for the trigger name and otherwise answers 201
Session counters are readable over HTTP

rationale.teaches: A dependency generator that closes its session on every path: try/finally around the yield, one session per request, no swallowed HTTPException, and validation before commit.
rationale.why: A session leak never fails the request that caused it; it exhausts the pool later. The fixture observes close calls and exception propagation directly, turning a delayed production failure into an immediate red.

ops.docstring: Item service that counts the sessions it opens and closes, to prove none leak.

ops.stmt: from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, Session, mapped_column, sessionmaker

ops.source:
class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    """Declarative base shared by every table in this module."""

class Item(Base):
    """A persisted catalog item."""

    __tablename__ = "items"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True, index=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(nullable=False)

class SessionMetrics:
    """Process-wide counters of sessions opened and closed."""

    created: int = 0
    closed: int = 0

def reset_db() -> None:
    """Recreate every table and zero the session counters."""
    Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)
    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
    SessionMetrics.created = 0
    SessionMetrics.closed = 0

session_factory = sessionmaker(
    class_=TrackedSession,
    autocommit=False,
    autoflush=False,
    bind=engine,
)

def get_db() -> Generator[Session, None, None]:
    """Open one counted session per request and always close it."""
    SessionMetrics.created += 1
    db = session_factory()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

class ItemResponse(BaseModel):
    """Item representation returned to clients."""

    id: int
    name: str

    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

@app.post("/items", status_code=201, response_model=ItemResponse)
def create_item(payload: ItemCreate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)) -> Item:
    """Persist a new item and return it."""
    item = Item(name=payload.name)
    db.add(item)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(item)
    return item

candidates.why_wrong: When the route raises, the statement after the yield never runs and the session is left open.
get_db returns the session instead of yielding it, so FastAPI never runs teardown and close is never called.
One module-level session is shared by every request, so state and failed transactions bleed across requests.
An HTTPException raised by the route is swallowed inside the dependency, so the client never sees the intended status.
The invalid item is committed before the validation error is raised, so the database keeps a row the client was told was rejected.
